items: Focus is also known as the Hypocenter; the Epicenter lies directly above it on the surface at a 90-degree angle.
Shallow-focus earthquakes (0–70 km depth) cause the highest intensity of surface shaking and structural damage.
Focal depth rarely exceeds 700 km because rocks at greater depths deform plastically under high temperature and pressure.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The focus (or hypocenter) is the point inside the Earth where seismic energy is first released during an earthquake.
The epicenter is the point on the Earth's surface located directly vertical to the focus, experiencing seismic waves first.
Earthquakes are categorized by focal depth: shallow (0–70 km), intermediate (70–300 km), and deep (300–700 km).
Shallow-focus earthquakes account for over 80% of total seismic energy release and cause the greatest surface devastation.
Deep-focus earthquakes occur primarily in subduction zones along Wadati-Benioff zones where oceanic crust sinks into the mantle.
